quote: Case I : θ1 < θ2. Let X~GIW(α, θ1 , λ, β) and Y~GIW(α, θ2 , λ, β). ... Since θ1 < θ2, d/dx [gX (y)/gY (y)] < 0. Hence, gX (y)/gY (y) is decreasing in y . That is X ≤lr Y . The remaining statement follow from the implication (32).
family: GIW (inverse truncated negative binomial Weibull / generalized inverse Weibull), pdf g(y; α, θ, λ, β) = αθ(1 − α)θ θβλβ y−(β+1) e−(λ/y)β / {(1 − αθ)[1 − (1 − α)e−(λ/y)β]θ+1}, Eq. (19)
compared: parameter θ1 vs θ2; α, λ, β common

hypotheses.text: Let X~GIW(α, θ1 , λ, β) and Y~GIW(α, θ2 , λ, β)
hypotheses.formal: X ~ GIW(α, θ1, λ, β), Y ~ GIW(α, θ2, λ, β)

hypotheses.text: X ≤rhr Y ⇐ X ≤lr Y ⇒ X ≤hr Y ⇒ X ≤st Y (32)
hypotheses.formal: lr order implies hr, st and rhr orders

conclusion.direction: X <=lr Y, hence also X <=hr Y, X <=st Y, X <=rhr Y via implication (32)

quantifiers: α, θ1, θ2, λ, β in the GIW parameter space (α, θ, λ, β > 0); all y > 0
ambiguity: Result is an unnumbered 'Case I' in Section 4.7, not a labeled theorem. The density ratio is printed with (1 − α2), (1 − α1) factors whose subscript placement is hard to parse in the text layer; the derivative expression contains garbled sub/superscripts (αθ vs αθ-terms). 'The remaining statement follow' [sic].
